meta.schwerpunkt: Investigate how reconciliation was done ad-hoc in prior sessions; produce a proposal for how reconciliation should be formalized

observations.fact: The 40-agent session (Z1IhGrcgGO, 2026-03-17 through 2026-03-19) used ad-hoc reconciliation at three distinct points: (1) L2040: commander asked to 'consolidate this prompt, and our recent conversation into a single clarifying set of questions'; (2) L2391: commander's major Schwerpunkt pivot asking the S3 to 'think hard using lots of tokens with everything you have in context about what i as the user should instruct you to do next'; (3) L3098+L3105+L3112+L3134: a four-turn cascade where commander asked for progressively deeper consolidated responses with reverse-chronological conversation audit, framework mapping, and glossary cross-referencing.

In the 40-agent session, reconciliation was ALWAYS initiated by the commander, never by the S3 independently. The S3 never said 'we should reconcile the findings from these parallel agents before proceeding.' The commander had to interrupt, redirect, and explicitly request synthesis at every reconciliation point.
observations.source: 40agent-human-messages.md — no instance of agent-initiated reconciliation found in 165 human messages

observations.fact: The 40-agent session used two reconciliation methods: (a) INLINE SYNTHESIS by the S3 itself (L2391 scope-creep analysis, L3098-L3134 four-turn consolidated responses) where the S3 burned tokens thinking with all context already loaded, and (b) SUBAGENT DELEGATION for specific investigations (e.g., S2 briefing cluster analysis agent #35, S2 session state audit agent #30, S2 scope-creep framework agent #19). Neither method was governed — the choice was situational.

This session (5HyCwPtSDH) formalized reconciliation as a 4-phase multi-agent mission: Phase 1a (parallel S2 consolidation of 7 AARs into ranked proposals), Phase 1b (filing briefs for glossary/incidents), Phase 1c (framework proposals), Phase 2-4 (S3 operations, S1 admin, session AAR). The S3 self-critiqued: it executed Phase 1a-c INLINE rather than delegating S2 subagents, citing that 'all 7 AARs, running estimate, and briefings already in context — delegating would have required subagents to re-read everything' (session-aar.json SO-6).
observations.source: session-aar.json SO-6, s2a-consolidated-proposals.json meta.method, running-estimate.json D12

observations.fact: The planning brief decision #26 governs S2 timing: 'S2 spawned at plan start (intelligence preparation) and plan end (findings consolidation).' Component (6): 'S2 consolidation: read .aitools/channel/, cross-reference, discard resolved, prepare outstanding briefs.' This is the closest existing governance to reconciliation — but it covers a SINGLE plan's findings within a SINGLE session, not cross-session or cross-mission reconciliation.

Decision #36 (Operational Learning) defines a 16-component pipeline: '(12) Pipeline: execution completes -> S3 delegates to S2 -> S2 invokes /debrief -> AAR produced in channel -> user validates proposals -> session ends -> channel-archive.sh archives high-severity -> harvest-session.sh archives scratch -> session-archive.sh archives transcript + auto-commit/push -> next session: S2 reads approved decisions (intelligence prep).' Reconciliation does NOT appear in this pipeline. The gap: what happens when MULTIPLE S2 AARs exist from PARALLEL missions and they need to be merged into coherent proposals?

The running estimate from this session (running-estimate.json v4) includes decision D-PER-SESSION-ESTIMATES which specifies a reconciliation algorithm for running estimates: 'UNION for arrays, LAST-UPDATED-WINS for scalars, MOST-ADVANCED-STATUS for enums.' This is DATA reconciliation (merging JSON documents), not INTELLIGENCE reconciliation (synthesizing findings from parallel investigations into coherent proposals). The two reconciliation types are distinct.

The filing briefs (s2b-filing-briefs.json) include a draft glossary definition for 'reconciliation': 'Merging per-session operational state into a single carry-forward artifact using a deterministic algorithm.' This definition covers only DATA reconciliation, not the INTELLIGENCE reconciliation that was this session's primary innovation. The term as drafted is too narrow.

The session AAR insight SI-2 states: 'RECONCILIATION IS THE MISSING PHASE IN THE MISSION COMMAND FRAMEWORK. Decision #3 covers delegation (briefing agents) and communication (SITREP/FINDING). Decision #26 covers S2 timing (start/end of plan). But there is no governed phase for RECONCILING the outputs of multiple parallel investigations into coherent proposals.' It recommends: triggered after parallel S2 investigations return, executed inline (synthesis of data already in context), produces ranked proposals with conflict analysis.

In the 40-agent session, the commander's four-turn reconciliation cascade (L3098-L3134) produced the most strategically valuable output of the entire 3-day session: the Lagebeurteilung concept, blast radius analysis, lifecycle transition framework, delegation duty expansions, and the /handoff skill improvements. This ad-hoc reconciliation sequence — prompted by the commander discovering the exit code 1 issue and asking 'what did we miss?' — was MORE productive than the 40 preceding subagent missions combined in terms of governance output.
observations.source: 40agent-human-messages.md L3098-L3134, cross-referenced with handoff-prompt-v2.md and /handoff SKILL.md

observations.fact: The 40-agent session had no running estimate. The S3 tracked state informally in conversation context. When the commander asked for consolidation (L2391), the S3 had to reconstruct state from conversation history — a process that took significant token burn and produced the session-state-audit subagent. This is the problem that led to the running estimate design (decision #50) in subsequent sessions.

Non-aitools project sessions in the dotprofile archives (grizzlies: 2 sessions, customers: appears in directory listing, and 20+ other projects) show no evidence of multi-agent reconciliation patterns. The grizzlies sessions are small (829KB and 3.4MB). Multi-agent orchestration and reconciliation appear to be aitools-specific patterns driven by the harness's complexity and the commander's progressive framework development.

insights.analysis: RECONCILIATION IS COMMANDER-INITIATED BECAUSE NO TRIGGER EXISTS IN THE GOVERNANCE. The S3 never independently triggers reconciliation because: (1) Decision #26 only says 'consolidation at plan end' — a single S2 pass, not a multi-pass synthesis operation. (2) The delegation duty has no 'RECONCILE-CHECK' component analogous to the proposed 'PATTERN-CHECK' (component 10). (3) No rule says 'after N parallel investigations return, reconcile before proceeding.' The commander fills this governance gap manually every time. The fix is explicit: add reconciliation as a governed phase with trigger conditions.

THERE ARE TWO TYPES OF RECONCILIATION, AND THEY HAVE DIFFERENT OPTIMAL EXECUTION PATTERNS. (A) DATA RECONCILIATION: merging structured state (running estimates, JSON registries) using deterministic algorithms (UNION, LAST-UPDATED-WINS, MOST-ADVANCED-STATUS). This is mechanical and should be automated (hooks, scripts). (B) INTELLIGENCE RECONCILIATION: synthesizing findings, proposals, and insights from parallel investigations into ranked themes with convergence analysis and conflict identification. This requires judgment and should be executed by an agent with full context. The session AAR correctly notes that intelligence reconciliation should be INLINE (agent already has context) while data reconciliation should be AUTOMATED (deterministic, no judgment needed).

THE GLOSSARY TERM 'RECONCILIATION' IS DRAFTED TOO NARROWLY. The current draft (s2b-filing-briefs.json) defines reconciliation as only data reconciliation. It needs to cover both types: data reconciliation (algorithmic merging of structured state) AND intelligence reconciliation (human/agent synthesis of parallel investigation outputs into coherent proposals). Without the intelligence reconciliation definition, the governance gap identified in SI-2 remains unaddressed even after the term is filed.

INLINE SYNTHESIS IS THE CORRECT PATTERN FOR INTELLIGENCE RECONCILIATION — BUT ONLY WHEN THE S3 ALREADY HAS ALL CONTEXT. This session's S3 was correct: delegating S2 subagents to re-read 7 AARs they had already read would waste tokens and lose the cross-AAR convergence visibility that comes from having everything in one context window. However, the 40-agent session's four-turn reconciliation cascade (L3098-L3134) shows a different scenario: the commander had to force the S3 to BURN TOKENS THINKING rather than delegating. The lesson: reconciliation is a token-intensive synthesis operation. It should not be delegated to subagents (they lack cross-investigation context), but it should be TRIGGERED so the S3 knows to do it rather than waiting for the commander to ask.

RECONCILIATION IS WHERE THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE GOVERNANCE DECISIONS EMERGE. The 40-agent session's reconciliation cascade (L3098-L3134) produced Lagebeurteilung, blast radius, lifecycle transition, delegation duty expansions — all from the commander asking 'what did we miss?' after a failure. This session's reconciliation mission produced 10 ranked proposal themes from 38 proposals, 3 conflict resolutions, 3 framework proposals, and 8 new governed terms. The pattern: reconciliation is not just 'clean up after parallel work' — it is the point where parallel investigation surfaces CONVERGENCE that would be invisible from any single investigation thread. Without reconciliation, M1 and M4 never discover they independently converged on the .gitignore fix.

proposals.title: Formalize reconciliation as a governed phase in Mission Command
proposals.targetArtifact: Planning brief decision #3 (amendment) + .claude/rules/delegation.md (new section) + reference/framework-mission-command.md (new section)
proposals.description: Add reconciliation as the sixth component of plan execution coordination (after S2 start, batch execution, inter-batch channel reads, S2 end, S1 filing). Reconciliation is triggered when parallel investigations return, and its output feeds the S2 consolidation and the running estimate.
proposals.trigger: When 2+ parallel S2 investigations complete. When the running estimate has findings from multiple sessions. At handoff time when multiple work streams have produced proposals.
proposals.executionPattern: INLINE by the orchestrating S3 (not delegated to subagents). The S3 already has all investigation outputs in context. Token-intensive synthesis, not tool-intensive research.
outputs: Ranked proposal themes with convergence scores (which AARs agree on each proposal)
Conflict analysis (proposals that contradict each other, with resolution recommendation)
Filing briefs (terms for glossary, candidates for incidents)
proposals.effort: LOW — amending existing decisions and adding a section to the framework reference
proposals.leverage: HIGH — addresses the primary governance gap identified in this session's AAR (SI-2)

proposals.title: Split 'reconciliation' glossary term into two definitions
proposals.description: Replace the single 'reconciliation' draft term with two governed terms: (A) 'data reconciliation' — algorithmic merging of structured state using deterministic rules (UNION, LAST-UPDATED-WINS, MOST-ADVANCED-STATUS). Applied to: running estimates, channel state, harvest manifests. (B) 'intelligence reconciliation' — synthesis of parallel investigation outputs into ranked proposals with convergence analysis and conflict identification. Applied to: AARs from parallel missions, findings from parallel S2 agents, proposals from multiple sessions.
proposals.rationale: The two reconciliation types have different execution patterns (automated vs inline), different triggers (hook/script vs S3 decision), different outputs (merged JSON vs ranked proposals), and different quality criteria (deterministic correctness vs analytical completeness). Treating them as one term creates ambiguity about WHICH reconciliation is needed at any given point.
proposals.leverage: MEDIUM — prevents the ambiguity identified in I-3

proposals.title: Add RECONCILE-CHECK as delegation duty component 11
proposals.description: After parallel investigations return (PATTERN-CHECK says to use parallel S2), the delegating agent MUST ask: 'Do these outputs need reconciliation before proceeding?' If yes, execute intelligence reconciliation inline before delegating the next phase. This makes reconciliation a STRUCTURAL part of the delegation workflow, not an ad-hoc commander intervention.
proposals.trigger: After any parallel investigation pattern completes
proposals.antiPattern: Proceeding directly from parallel investigation outputs to implementation without checking for convergence and conflicts (what this session would have done without the reconciliation mission)
proposals.effort: LOW — one component addition to an existing duty
proposals.leverage: HIGH — prevents the governance gap from recurring in future multi-agent sessions

proposals.title: Create a reconciliation template for the consolidated proposals format
proposals.description: Standardize the output format of intelligence reconciliation, based on what this session produced (s2a-consolidated-proposals.json). The format: meta (producer, method, session), convergenceRanking (ranked themes with convergence scores, proposal references, target artifacts, best formulation, effort, leverage, planning brief decision links), conflictAnalysis (conflicting proposals with resolution), proposalsByTargetArtifact (reverse index), executionSequence (dependency-aware waves).
proposals.rationale: This session's reconciliation produced a well-structured output that could serve as a template. Without a template, each reconciliation will reinvent the format, losing the structural convergence analysis that was the key insight.
proposals.effort: LOW — the format already exists, just needs to be codified as a template
proposals.leverage: MEDIUM — ensures reconciliation outputs are comparable across sessions

proposals.title: Reconciliation should be part of /handoff, NOT a separate /reconcile skill
proposals.description: Reconciliation is the intelligence analysis that feeds the handoff. It is NOT a standalone activity — it serves the handoff's purpose (capture everything for the accepting session). Adding it to /handoff as a pre-step or integrating it into the Lagebeurteilung assessment is the correct placement. A separate /reconcile skill would create a process that could be invoked without a handoff, producing orphaned reconciliation outputs that never feed into session transitions. The /handoff skill already has the Lagebeurteilung (situation assessment) — intelligence reconciliation is the most demanding part of that assessment when the session has had parallel investigations.
proposals.rationale: This session's experience: the reconciliation mission WAS the final pre-handoff assessment. The session AAR, consolidated proposals, and dashboard were all /handoff outputs. Reconciliation is the content; handoff is the container.
proposals.effort: MEDIUM — requires updating /handoff to include reconciliation as an explicit sub-step
proposals.leverage: HIGH — prevents skill proliferation, keeps reconciliation connected to its purpose

proposals.title: Document the inline synthesis pattern as an orchestration pattern
proposals.targetArtifact: reference/orchestration-patterns.md (proposed in M9 AAR), planning brief amendment
proposals.description: Add INLINE-SYNTHESIS as the 6th orchestration pattern alongside the 5 identified in M9 AAR. Trigger: when the orchestrating agent already has all investigation outputs in context and needs to perform cross-investigation analysis. Composition: S3 burns tokens thinking (no delegation), produces structured synthesis output, optionally delegates verification. Anti-pattern: delegating synthesis to a subagent that must re-read everything the S3 already has. Example: this session Phase 1a (inline consolidation of 7 AARs into 10 ranked themes).
proposals.rationale: This session proved the pattern works and identified its trigger condition. It complements PARALLEL-INVESTIGATE (which produces the raw outputs that INLINE-SYNTHESIS then reconciles).
proposals.leverage: MEDIUM — codifies a pattern already demonstrated twice (40-agent session L3098-L3134, this session Phase 1a)

crossSessionPatterns.summary: Reconciliation appeared in 2 of the 7+ sessions examined. Both instances were in aitools (the most complex project). Non-aitools projects in the dotprofile archives showed no reconciliation patterns, likely because they do not generate parallel multi-agent investigations.

whatWorked: Structuring reconciliation as a multi-phase mission with explicit Schwerpunkt
Inline synthesis for the intelligence reconciliation (S3 already had all AARs in context)
Explicit convergence scoring (counting how many AARs agreed on each proposal)
Conflict analysis as a separate output (not just picking winners)
Execution sequencing as a reconciliation output (wave ordering)
Connecting proposals back to planning brief decisions (traceability)
whatDidNotWork: The reconciliation agent self-critiqued: used inline synthesis instead of delegating S2s. However, the investigation shows inline synthesis IS the correct pattern for intelligence reconciliation when context is loaded. The self-critique was wrong — the execution was correct.
No explicit trigger existed — the commander had to define the reconciliation mission ad-hoc
The reconciliation mission was the LAST mission in the session, when it should have been triggered automatically after the parallel investigations (M1-M9) completed
comparisonToThisSession.inlineSynthesisVerdict: CORRECT PATTERN for intelligence reconciliation. Delegating would lose the cross-investigation convergence visibility. The S3 in this session was right to execute Phases 1a-c inline, despite self-critiquing the choice.

formalizationProposal.shouldReconciliationBeAGovernedPhase: YES — it is the missing phase between parallel investigation and handoff/execution. Without it, convergence between parallel investigations is invisible.
formalizationProposal.shouldThereBeAReconcileSkill: NO — reconciliation is a step within /handoff (Lagebeurteilung + intelligence synthesis = reconciliation). A separate skill would create orphaned outputs.
formalizationProposal.shouldItBePartOfHandoff: YES — reconciliation is the most demanding part of the Lagebeurteilung when the session has had parallel investigations. The handoff skill already has the framework; it needs an explicit reconciliation sub-step.
inputs: AARs from completed missions (per-mission structured learning)
Running estimate (current session state, findings, assumptions)
Planning brief (decisions that proposals must be coherent with)
Channel messages (SITREPs and FINDINGs from delegation)
Prior session handoffs (context from earlier sessions)
outputs: Consolidated proposals with convergence ranking (s2a format)
Filing briefs for glossary terms and incident candidates (s2b format)
Framework proposals for harness evolution (s2c format)

provenanceMapping.MDMP_Step7_OrdersProduction: Reconciliation is the synthesis of analysis into orders. MDMP Step 7 takes COA analysis results and produces the operations order. Our reconciliation takes parallel investigation AARs and produces consolidated proposals (the 'order' for the accepting session).
provenanceMapping.HoshinKanri_Catchball: Reconciliation embodies the Catchball principle — bidirectional negotiation between what the investigations found (bottom-up) and what the planning brief decided (top-down). Proposals must be coherent with existing decisions while incorporating new findings.
provenanceMapping.OODA_Decide: Reconciliation maps to the DECIDE phase of OODA. After OBSERVE (missions) and ORIENT (AARs), DECIDE synthesizes into actionable proposals. The ACT phase is the accepting session implementing the proposals.
provenanceMapping.Lagebeurteilung: Already adopted. Reconciliation IS the Lagebeurteilung applied to multi-investigation sessions. The mandatory category walkthrough (forces, terrain, time, logistics, assumptions) structured the 40-agent session's most valuable output.

discrepanciesNoted: The running estimate at running-estimate.json was read. It lists D-PER-SESSION-ESTIMATES as 'decided' — but this decision covers only DATA reconciliation. INTELLIGENCE reconciliation is not covered by any decision in the running estimate or planning brief.

The session AAR insight SI-2 identifies reconciliation as the missing phase, but the session AAR itself was produced BY the reconciliation phase — circular: the phase that identifies the gap IS the gap. This is the bootstrap problem applied to operational learning.

The planning brief decision #26 component (6) says 'S2 consolidation: read .aitools/channel/, cross-reference, discard resolved, prepare outstanding briefs.' This is intelligence reconciliation for a single plan. The gap is: what happens when MULTIPLE plans or sessions need their outputs reconciled? Decision #26 assumes one plan per session.
frameworkConnections: Operational Learning (proposed, decision #36) — reconciliation is the CONSOLIDATE step in the 7-step cycle: OBSERVE -> SURFACE -> CONSOLIDATE -> PROPOSE -> DECIDE -> EMBED -> VERIFY
Mission Command (proposed, decision #3) — reconciliation fills the gap between delegation (briefing agents) and handoff (transitioning to accepting session). It is the intelligence analysis phase.

Three-layer governance (existing) — reconciliation is governed at the Prevention layer (this investigation's proposals), detected at the Detection layer (delegation duty component 11 = RECONCILE-CHECK), and audited at the Audit layer (/audit skill checking for unreconciled parallel outputs).

P-3: Add RECONCILE-CHECK as delegation duty component 11
P-4: Codify reconciliation template from this session's s2a format
